The **NASBO project** (NASBO-projektet) is a British research study referenced in the 2024–2025 annual report from the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) regarding the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) [^src1]. Within the context of evaluating quality indicators for treatment speed and high-risk patient safety, the study is cited as international evidence demonstrating that variations in clinical practice and resource allocation have a direct impact on patient outcomes [^src1]. 

By highlighting these findings, the NASBO project serves as a key justification for quality improvement initiatives in the Danish acute surgical sector [^src1]. Specifically, the study's conclusions are used to underscore the critical need for increased [[standardisering]] and the systematic sharing of best practices across regions, particularly those with lower performance metrics [^src1].
